hook: You've started the same habit at least a dozen times. Here's what that means.
body:
**You've started this before. The gym. The early mornings. The phone off the table.**

Maybe a dozen times. Maybe more.

And every time, you were serious. Every time, you meant it. And every time, within two weeks, it was gone.

Here's what that does to a man over time. It's not just the habit that breaks. It's the contract you have with yourself. Every time you commit to something and don't follow through, your brain logs that. Not consciously — silently. It updates its prediction about what you will actually do next time.

Self-trust is not a feeling. It is a credit score. Built from every commitment you have kept or broken with yourself. And most men are operating on a score so low that they don't fully believe their own intentions anymore — even when they make them.

The way out of this is not to make bigger commitments. It is to make smaller ones and keep them without exception.

One kept commitment, consistently, begins to change the record. Not dramatically. Just — the next data point is different.

That is where it starts.

Follow for more.
visual_direction: Marcus speaking directly to camera, no expression change, measured delivery. Slight pause before "Self-trust is not a feeling." Let that line breathe.
caption_hook: Every commitment you've broken with yourself has been logged. Here's what that cost you.
tiktok_caption: Every commitment you've broken with yourself has been logged. Self-trust isn't a feeling — it's a credit score. Here's how to rebuild it.
